Summary:

Data source overview: The reviewed text is a concise survey of secure and private artificial-intelligence techniques for deep neural networks (DNNs), covering threats during training (poisoning), inference (evasion/adversarial examples) and post-training privacy attacks (model inversion or dishonest service providers). It outlines families of defences—data sanitisation, robustness training, model/parameter masking, differential privacy and homomorphic encryption—together with high-level comments on their advantages and challenges.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[82]

Inference strategy justification: The paper is a high-level review without experimental sections, so I inferred intermediate reasoning steps (e.g., specific implementation mechanisms and validation evidence) from commonly cited literature examples that the review alludes to. All inferred links are marked with confidence 2–3 and rationale notes.

Extraction completeness explanation: Every distinct risk, analysis, insight, design rationale, mechanism, evidence and intervention mentioned or implied in the source has been captured and threaded into three interconnected causal-interventional pathways (poisoning, evasion, privacy). A single top-level risk node interconnects the branches, ensuring a fully connected fabric. Nodes are named at optimal granularity for cross-source merging.

Key limitations:
• The review text is short; empirical details had to be inferred, lowering confidence.
• Validation evidence nodes are generic because no specific metrics were given.
• Homomorphic-encryption details (CKKS scheme) are typical rather than explicit in the text.
